# Verification analysis: etcd-member-replacement-rhel10

Job: `2026-09-04__20-11-34`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Run a three-member etcd cluster across `node1`, `node2`, and `node3` holding
> application keys.
>
> The member on `node3` is permanently lost and its data cannot be recovered.
> Replace it with a working member on that same system so the cluster is back to
> three healthy members with the existing keys intact.

## Trial `etcd-member-replacement-rhel10__392E3KJ`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built a working 3-member etcd v3.7.1 cluster on node1/node2/node3, loaded application keys, then faithfully simulated node3's permanent, unrecoverable member loss (service stopped/disabled, data directory wiped), removed the stale member while preserving 2-node quorum and verifying key integrity, and added/bootstrapped a new node3 member in existing-cluster mode. Final verification shows all 3 members 'started' and healthy with matching raft applied indices and all application keys present on the rebuilt node3 endpoint, directly satisfying the task contract. The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was also executed on all three nodes with pre-restart healthy baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot IDs (cross-checked against the fixed before/after global snapshots), and confirmed post-restart cluster health, quorum, and data recovery. The only hygiene concern is unremoved etcd installation build artifacts left in /tmp on all three nodes.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.900 | 46/3 (+9 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Three-member etcd cluster established across node1/node2/node3 holding application keys
  - **Why:** member list shows all 3 members (node1/node2/node3) in 'started' state, endpoint health true for all three endpoints, and /app/config/db_host, /app/config/feature_flag_x, /app/counters/orders written and read back successfully from node3's endpoint.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-8fdc90cce4f94cdf`, `cmd-7a3fb7b601f140a8`, `cmd-23fa8322523747f0`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** node3's original member permanently lost with unrecoverable data (simulated failure)
  - **Why:** etcd stopped and disabled on node3, /var/lib/etcd contents removed, directory confirmed empty, directly demonstrating a destroyed, unrecoverable member on node3.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-7519b8f2f7674b66`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** Stale node3 member removed from cluster while quorum and existing application keys are preserved
  - **Why:** member remove on the dead node3 ID succeeded, member list afterward shows only node1/node2 both 'started' and healthy (2-node quorum maintained), and /app/* keys were still readable, showing no data loss.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-eecd1202c8bd479d`
- **R4 — Satisfied:** New working member added on node3 and cluster restored to 3 healthy members with existing keys intact
  - **Why:** member add for node3 succeeded, a fresh etcd instance was bootstrapped there in existing-cluster mode and came active; subsequent member list/health/status show 3 started+healthy members with matching raft applied index (23) across all three endpoints, and /app/* keys were read directly from the rebuilt node3 endpoint, confirming data replication onto the new member.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1a769962ba974c63`, `cmd-2ac2254988ce4b4d`, `cmd-355865ff796a4419`, `cmd-3bae661297cb4c05`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. All state-changing commands trace to a clear purpose (package install, user/dir setup, firewalld/systemd config, cluster bootstrap, simulated failure, member replacement, restart protocol). One transient failure (cmd-6e15969e41844870, node1 etcd enable --now timing out during initial 3-way quorum formation) was a normal bootstrap hiccup, immediately followed by a successful activation (cmd-a62cf5c2fc59439e) and is not a problematic mutation. The main hygiene deduction is leftover build artifacts (/tmp/etcd.tar.gz and the extracted /tmp/etcd-v3.7.1-linux-amd64 directory) left in place on all three nodes after binary installation (visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot for node1/node2/node3) rather than being cleaned up; this is bounded, low-risk residue but was never reverted. No failed services, no unsafe firewall exposure (only etcd-client/etcd-server added, matching the cluster's own needs), and no package-manager damage were observed in the after_executor snapshots.

Hygiene evidence: `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`, `cmd-6e15969e41844870`, `cmd-a62cf5c2fc59439e`
